query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A precisely controlled aging heat treatment will induce the in‐situ precipitation of a fine, ductile secondary phase along grain boundaries in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38, thereby arresting crack propagation and enhancing mechanical integrity without diminishing the large caloric response.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with a homogeneous microstructure that exhibits a strong caloric effect but suffers from poor crack resistance.
generation.intervention: Apply a targeted aging heat treatment at an optimized temperature and time to promote nucleation and growth of a fine, ductile precipitate phase.
generation.conditions: Tested under applied magnetic and pressure fields within the operational temperature range of the caloric effect, and under load conditions similar to those experienced during practical deployment (compressive loads up to or exceeding previously measured baselines).
generation.structural_mediator: Finely dispersed ductile precipitates (likely an Fe-rich or related phase intrinsic to the base composition) along grain boundaries and within the matrix.
generation.mechanism: The heat treatment induces phase separation where a minor, ductile secondary phase precipitates at grain boundaries, thereby reinforcing intergranular cohesion. This microstructural modification impedes crack initiation and propagation while leaving the primary phase (responsible for the strong caloric response) largely unaltered.
generation.predicted_outcome: The heat-treated alloy exhibits a significant increase in mechanical integrity (e.g., a compressive strength improvement by at least 20% relative to the untreated state) while maintaining its high caloric response (with less than a 5% reduction in caloric magnitude).
generation.baseline: Untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy that shows high caloric response but poor mechanical integrity, evidenced by low compressive strength and a propensity to crack.
generation.boundary: The intervention is expected to be effective under operating conditions where the applied magnetic and pressure fields activate the caloric effect. Its success is bounded to the thermal and field regimes typical for such materials (e.g., moderate temperatures, magnetic fields up to a few Tesla, and compressive loads within the alloy's elastic limits). The treatment must be calibrated so as not to excessively coarsen the microstructure or alter the phase balance that drives the caloric response.
generation.uncertainty: The identity and distribution of the precipitated phase and its stability under cyclic field and mechanical loads remain to be confirmed experimentally. There is also uncertainty whether the aging treatment will uniformly improve toughness without inadvertently affecting the caloric entropy change.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy samples: one set following the standard casting process and one set subjected to the proposed aging heat treatment. Conduct mechanical tests (compressive strength, fracture toughness) and caloric performance evaluations under identical magnetic and pressure fields. Use microstructural characterization (using SEM/TEM) to verify the presence, size, and distribution of the ductile precipitates.
measurements: Caloric response (e.g., isothermal entropy change or adiabatic temperature change) under applied fields
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the heat-treated samples do not exhibit at least a 20% improvement in mechanical integrity (e.g., compressive strength) without more than a 5% reduction in the caloric response compared to the untreated samples, or if the fine ductile precipitates are not observed or are unevenly distributed, then the hypothesis is falsified.
